page: Microsoft Azure F48ams_v7 is an AMD-based virtual machine configured under Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by a dedicated 48-core AMD EPYC 9V45 processor using the x86_64 architecture, running at up to 4.5 GHz with a single thread per core (48 vCPUs on 48 physical cores). The architecture integrates 48 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core cluster, alongside modern instruction sets including AVX-512 (F, VNNI, BF16), AES, and SHA_NI.

The instance delivers an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio, featuring 384.0 GB of RAM (8.0 GB per core). It does not include an onboard GPU, and local disk storage is not bundled (listed as None), requiring external remote persistent storage for persistent operating system and data requirements. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned.

Benchmark measurements place the F48ams_v7 in the top tier for raw processor and memory operations. It recorded a Geekbench multi-core score of 29,329.0 and a single-core score of 2,865.0, supported by a PassMark CPU score of 98,569.22 and stress-ng multi-core performance of 175,169.62. Memory operations remain equally high, registering 8,968.86 GB/sec cached small-block read bandwidth, 172.68 GB/sec uncached large-block write throughput, and 130.96 million operations per second on Redis SET tests.

Because physical cores are dedicated without simultaneous multithreading (SMT), CPU execution predictability is maintained under sustained concurrent utilization. Cost efficiency scales well for high-throughput computing combined with large in-memory footprints, bypassing the need for higher-tier hyperthreaded instances. The architecture is suited for large in-memory databases, Redis caches, CI/CD compilation pipelines, intensive data transformations, and CPU-based small-to-medium machine learning inference.
description: Microsoft Azure F48ams_v7 is a high-capacity virtual machine built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz. It features 48 dedicated physical cores with single-threading (48 vCPUs) and 384.0 GB of system RAM, providing an 8:1 memory-to-core density. It lacks integrated GPUs and bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage. Benchmark testing demonstrates top-tier computational performance, with a Geekbench multi-core rating of 29,329.0, a PassMark CPU rating of 98,569.22, and write bandwidth reaching 172.68 GB/sec on large uncached memory blocks. The instance is suited for enterprise in-memory databases, Redis instances, intensive CI/CD compilation, and large-scale data manipulation workloads requiring dedicated processing cores.
